card.name: Start of words in military metaphors
card.fires_on: The first piece of a word split into parts, or a word that opens a figurative phrase, where the next part is a war or weapon term (armaments, beachhead, arteries). Seen in general news and essay text.

modes.label: Split word start
modes.description: The opening piece of a longer word broken into parts, such as arm in armaments.
modes.example: So why would Syria have such<< arm>>aments?

modes.label: Figurative phrase
modes.description: A word inside a metaphor that borrows war or conflict imagery.
modes.example: Waterways were then the<< transportation>> arteries, and nowhere else in North America

card.writes: It suppresses weapon and war words, so it reduces the chance that the next word is about arms or fighting.
card.plain: It fires on the start of a word or phrase where a weapon or war word might come next, and it lowers that guess.
